1.c4 c6 2.Nf3.strategy: Develops the king's knight towards the centre, covering d4 and e5, and commits no pawn beyond c4. White keeps the choice of set-up open: a classical centre, a quiet build-up or a fianchetto. The price is that Black keeps a free hand too, so neither side forces the character of the game.

1.c4 c6 2.e4.strategy: Takes the centre with a pawn at once and fights for d5, the square the c6-pawn is meant to support. It aims at direct, open play with extra space, but Black can strike back at the centre straight away.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3.strategy: Develops the queen's knight, guards d5 and e4 and prepares to take the centre with either central pawn. It keeps White flexible but claims no space yet, so Black can occupy the centre first and the game stays a manoeuvring fight over the pawn structure.

1.c4 c6 2.d4.strategy: Claims the centre with a second pawn and puts the c4-pawn to work against d5. If Black takes space with ...d5, the game becomes a classical, strategic fight over the centre. The price is that d4 has only the queen behind it until a knight arrives, and Black may keep the centre flexible.

1.c4 c6 2.e3.strategy: Opens the f1-bishop and prepares d4, aiming for a quiet set-up. It is sound but passive: it shuts in the c1-bishop and no piece is out yet, so Black can take central space at once.

1.c4 c6 2.g3.strategy: Prepares Bg2 to press on d5 along the long diagonal, with quick development and castling to follow. It is sound but slow: no d- or e-pawn has moved, so Black can take the centre at once.

1.c4 c6 2.b3.strategy: Prepares Bb2 on the long diagonal, aimed at e5 and the kingside, and supports the c4-pawn so that ...dxc4 can be met by bxc4. The plan is sound but slow, as White does nothing to stop Black taking the centre, and Black gets it first.

1.c4 c6 2.d3.strategy: Prepares e4 and frees the c1-bishop, in a closed set-up built on a kingside fianchetto. It is solid but modest: the move neither fights for d5 nor takes space, so Black can build the centre at once.

1.c4 c6 2.b4.name: Polish Opening: Outflank Variation
1.c4 c6 2.b4.background: The same position arises from 1.b4 c6, the Outflank Variation of the Polish Opening. After 1.c4 c6, 2.b4 can serve as a surprise weapon against a player who knows little about the Polish Opening. The opening is not popular at the top level but still sees sporadic use: in May 2021 world champion Magnus Carlsen played it against Hikaru Nakamura and Wesley So in the online FTX Crypto Cup rapid tournament.
1.c4 c6 2.b4.strategy: Gains queenside space and prepares Bb2 on the long diagonal towards g7. The b4-pawn has no pawn support, though: 2...a5 and ...Qb6 attack it at once and ...e5 opens the f8-bishop against it, so White spends time holding b4 and c4 while Black builds the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.a3.strategy: Prepares b4, but spends a tempo on a rook-pawn move that develops nothing and does not contest d5. Black takes the centre with 2...d5 and develops without hindrance.

1.c4 c6 2.a4.strategy: Stops ...b5 and gains a little queenside space, but weakens b4 and develops nothing. Black takes the centre at once while White has no piece out.

1.c4 c6 2.f3.strategy: Takes f3 from the king's knight and opens the e1–h4 diagonal towards the king. The idea of e4 is slow, and 2...d5 takes the centre first.

1.c4 c6 2.f4.strategy: Gains kingside space and controls e5, but opens the e1–h4 diagonal towards the king and does nothing about Black winning central space at once.

1.c4 c6 2.h3.strategy: A waiting move that only takes g4 from the c8-bishop for later. It costs a tempo and does not stop 2...d5, so Black takes the centre while White has developed nothing.

1.c4 c6 2.Na3.strategy: Defends c4 and heads for c2, but on the rim the knight controls no central square, cannot use b5 because of the c6-pawn and blocks the a-pawn. Black takes the centre and develops freely.

1.c4 c6 2.Nh3.strategy: Heads for f4, but the knight sits on the rim instead of on f3, where it would cover d4 and e5. Once the c8-bishop is free it eyes h3, and a later ...Bxh3 gxh3 leaves White with doubled h-pawns for the bishop pair.

1.c4 c6 2.Qc2.strategy: Supports c4 and prepares e4, but brings the queen out before any minor piece. Black takes the centre with 2...d5 while White has developed nothing else.

1.c4 c6 2.Qb3.strategy: Eyes b7 down the b-file, but the c4-pawn blocks the queen's diagonal and no minor piece is out. Black takes the centre and can offer a queen trade, so White gains nothing for the early sortie.

1.c4 c6 2.Qa4.strategy: Eyes c6 and the a4–e8 diagonal without a real threat, since c6 is defended. Black takes the centre and develops at ease while the queen is left looking for a useful square.

1.c4 c6 2.c5.strategy: Gains queenside space but gives up the pressure on d5. Black can take the centre, or undermine the advanced pawn with ...b6, and it becomes a target with no pawn support behind it.

1.c4 c6 2.g4.strategy: Lunges forward without developing a piece and leaves the pawn loose: after 2...d5 the c8-bishop eyes g4, and White needs h3 or f3. The advance also weakens f4, h4 and the long diagonal.

1.c4 c6 2.h4.strategy: Gains kingside space but does nothing for the centre or development, and weakens g4 and g3 for good. Black takes the centre with 2...d5 and develops freely.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 d5.strategy: Claims the centre at once, with the c6-pawn guarding d5, so the c8-bishop stays free to come out on f5 or g4 before ...e6 closes it in. The cost is a solid but slightly passive structure and the question of when to release that bishop.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the king's knight, eyes d5 and e4 and keeps the central pawn moves in reserve. Black stays flexible and lets White show a plan first, at the cost of not yet claiming any central space.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 e6.strategy: Prepares ...d5 with a compact pawn triangle on c6, d5 and e6, but commits the e-pawn and shuts in the c8-bishop before it has come out. Sound, but less flexible than keeping the e-pawn at home and developing first.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 d6.strategy: Opens the c8-bishop's diagonal and prepares ...e5 with piece development. The push needs that preparation: 3.d4 e5? 4.dxe5 dxe5 5.Qxd8+ Kxd8 6.Nxe5 wins a pawn. Sound but passive, since White takes space in the centre at leisure.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 f5.strategy: Heads for a solid wall of pawns on c6, d5, e6 and f5, the c6-pawn backing the chain. It weakens e6 and the e8-h5 diagonal, and in that set-up the e5-square becomes a lasting hole for a white knight. Sound, but less natural than claiming the centre directly.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 g6.strategy: Prepares a fianchetto of the king's bishop, with the c6-pawn ready to support ...d5. It is sound but slow, and White can claim space in the centre before Black has a pawn there.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 c5.strategy: Pushes the c-pawn a second time. The position is a symmetrical English with White to move, so White is a tempo up, and Black has spent two moves on one pawn without developing a piece or taking central space.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 b6.strategy: Aims at ...Ba6 against c4, since on b7 the bishop would bite on its own c6-pawn, and it does nothing about the centre. White takes the centre, and simply defends c4 against ...Ba6.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 b5.strategy: Offers to trade the b-pawn for White's c-pawn, but after 3.cxb5 cxb5 the b5-pawn is a target that White's knight and queen can attack while developing. White gains time against it and builds the centre, while Black has developed nothing.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 a6.strategy: Prepares ...b5 but spends a tempo on the wing while the centre stands empty, so White takes space at once. The pawn does nothing for d5 or for development.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 a5.strategy: Stops b2-b4 but spends a tempo on an edge pawn, leaves the centre to White and helps no piece develop. White gains space in the centre with ease.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 h6.strategy: Takes g5 from a future Bg5 or Ng5, but spends a tempo on a pawn move before any piece is out. White builds the centre unopposed.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 h5.strategy: Advances a flank pawn without a plan, weakens g6 and the kingside cover and develops nothing. White simply builds the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 f6.strategy: Prepares ...e5 but takes f6 from the g8-knight and weakens e6 and the e8-h5 diagonal. The centre is still unclaimed, so White takes it and gains space.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 Na6.strategy: Heads for c7, where the knight would cover d5 and b5, but the trip costs two moves and the knight stands on the rim meanwhile. White takes the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 Nh6.strategy: Aims for f5, but the rim knight blocks the h-pawn and invites 3.d4, when Bxh6 threatens to double Black's pawns and a pawn advance in the centre drives the knight away from f5 with a gain of space.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 Qc7.strategy: Brings the queen out early to support ...e5, before any other piece is developed. White builds the centre at leisure, and after d4 a bishop on f4 can gain time against the queen.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 Qb6.strategy: Seems to hit b2, but the bishop on c1 guards it. The queen has no target while White develops and takes the centre at leisure.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 Qa5.strategy: Puts the queen on the a5-e1 diagonal, where it pins the d2-pawn for a moment but attacks nothing of value. White blocks the diagonal with 3.Nc3 and takes the centre at leisure, while Black has no piece out and no pawn in the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 e5.strategy: Leaves the pawn undefended: 3.Nxe5 wins it, and after 3...Qa5 the knight simply retreats to f3 with the extra pawn. Black gets too little for it.

1.c4 c6 2.Nf3 g5.strategy: Hangs the pawn, since nothing defends g5 and 3.Nxg5 takes it. It also loosens the kingside for good, and Black gets neither development nor an attack in return.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 d5.strategy: Takes the centre with the pawn that ...c6 supports and challenges c4 at once, while the c8-bishop stays free to develop outside the pawn chain. Black gets a solid structure with few weaknesses, but bringing the queenside pieces out is the difficulty.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 Nf6.strategy: Develops the knight and keeps ...d5 in reserve. Unlike 2...d5 it allows 3.e4, when 3...d5 4.e5 attacks the knight and gains space.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 e6.strategy: Prepares ...d5 with a solid pawn chain and opens the f8-bishop, but the c8-bishop is shut in behind the e6-pawn. White can also grab space at once.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 e5.strategy: Claims central space and keeps its development flexible. It is sound but not recommended: the c-pawn has taken c6 from the knight, so the e5-pawn needs support or has to advance.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 g6.strategy: Prepares ...Bg7 and a quiet kingside set-up. It is sound but not recommended: it is slower than 2...d5, and White can build a broad centre before Black strikes at it.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 d6.strategy: Prepares ...e5 behind a solid pawn on d6. It is sound but passive: it postpones the ...d5 that ...c6 prepared, and White holds more space in the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 Na6.strategy: Puts the knight on the rim, where it eyes b4 and c7 but leaves the centre alone. Bringing it to c7 to support ...d5 costs another move, and White takes the centre in the meantime.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 Qc7.strategy: Brings the queen out before any piece is developed. It prepares ...e5 but leaves the centre to White, who takes it with a free hand.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 Qb6.strategy: Eyes b2 and f2, but both are guarded (by the c1-bishop and the king), so nothing is threatened. White develops freely, and the queen can later be hit with a gain of time.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 Qa5.strategy: Eyes c3 and a2 without a real threat, since the knight is guarded by the b2- and d2-pawns and a2 by the rook. Black has developed nothing, and White builds the centre while keeping the queen from pinning the c3-knight against the king.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 Nh6.strategy: Heads for f5 from the rim, but 3.d4 opens the c1-h6 diagonal and threatens Bxh6, ruining the kingside pawns. If the knight reaches f5, 4.e4 hits it again with a gain of space.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 a6.strategy: Prepares ...b5 but spends a tempo on a pawn move that does nothing for the centre or development. White answers by taking space and the centre unopposed.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 a5.strategy: Gains a little queenside space and takes b4 from White's pieces, but leaves the centre and development alone. White takes the centre unopposed.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 b6.strategy: Prepares ...Bb7, but the c6-pawn already blocks the long diagonal, so the bishop would only look at its own pawn. The move does nothing to stop White taking the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 f6.strategy: Takes f6 from the g8-knight and weakens the e8-h5 diagonal, with only control of e5 in return. White takes the centre before Black has a real plan.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 f5.strategy: Stakes out e4 with the f-pawn, but weakens e6 and the e8-h5 diagonal and develops nothing. White can strike at once with 3.e4, and after 3...fxe4 4.Nxe4 the open diagonal gives the queen a check on h5.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 h6.strategy: Takes g5 away from White's bishop, but costs a tempo and brings no development. White takes the centre at leisure.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 h5.strategy: A flank advance that leaves g5 without pawn cover for good, since the h-pawn can no longer guard it from h6, and leaves the centre untouched. White takes the centre unopposed.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 c5.strategy: Moves the c-pawn a second time and reaches a symmetrical set-up, but with White to move instead of Black, so Black has lost a full tempo. The pawn also gives up the support for ...d5 that ...c6 provided.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 b5.strategy: Gambits a pawn that White simply takes: after 3.cxb5 cxb5 4.Nxb5 White is a clean pawn up, and 4...Qa5 only hits the knight, which retreats to c3.

1.c4 c6 2.Nc3 g5.strategy: Overextends: nothing guards the g5-pawn, and 3.d4 opens the bishop's diagonal with the threat of Bxg5. Defending it with ...h6 loosens the kingside further.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 d5.strategy: Takes the centre at once with a chain of pawns on c6 and d5, which leaves the c8-bishop free to develop outside it. The c4-pawn already presses on d5, but c6 holds it. The game is solid and strategic: White has the extra move, Black a sound structure and an active bishop.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 Nf6.strategy: Develops a knight that covers d5 and e4, so an immediate e4 would simply lose a pawn. Black keeps the choice of structure open, at the cost of leaving the centre to White for now: without a follow-up in the centre, White can build a broad pawn centre.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 e6.strategy: Prepares ...d5 with a solid triangle of pawns on c6, d5 and e6. It keeps the king safe and the structure sound, but the c8-bishop is shut in behind the pawns until a later pawn exchange or break frees it, and e4 stays available to White.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 d6.name: Queen's Pawn Game: Anglo-Slav Opening
1.c4 c6 2.d4 d6.strategy: Delays ...d5, opens the c8-bishop's diagonal and prepares ...e5. It is sound but passive: White gets more space, and Black must find the right moment to break.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 g6.strategy: Prepares ...Bg7 in a Modern-style set-up that watches the long diagonal and d4. It is sound but passive: Black has made no central thrust, so White can build a broad centre.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 f5.strategy: Takes e4 under control and plans a compact set-up behind the f-pawn. It weakens the e8-h5 diagonal and the e6-square, and the c8-bishop ends up shut in behind the e6-pawn, so it is playable but gives White easy development.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 Na6.strategy: Brings the knight to the rim, where it eyes b4 and c5 but does little for the centre and blocks the a-pawn. Without a central pawn move Black cedes space, and White builds a full centre.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 Qc7.strategy: Prepares ...e5, but the queen moves out before any minor piece and leaves the centre to White. An immediate ...e5 meets dxe5 Qxe5 and Nf3 with a tempo on the queen, and otherwise White builds the centre at leisure.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 Qb6.strategy: Eyes d4 and b2, but both are guarded and the queen is exposed: Nc3 and Na4, or c5 at once, drive it back with tempo while Black has no piece out and has not fought for the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 Qa5+.strategy: The check gains nothing: Bd2 blocks it with a threat on the queen, or Nc3 develops a piece, and Black must spend further moves on the queen with no piece developed and the centre left to White.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 Nh6.strategy: Heads for f5 to hit d4, but the knight on the rim is met by Bxh6 gxh6, which leaves Black with doubled, isolated h-pawns for the bishop pair. The centre belongs to White meanwhile.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 a6.strategy: Prepares ...b5 against c4, but it takes a tempo and develops nothing, so White has a free hand in the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 a5.strategy: Restrains a later b4 but is a slow rook-pawn move that develops nothing and gives up control of b6. White builds the centre at leisure.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 b6.strategy: Prepares ...Bb7, but the c6-pawn shuts that bishop in from the start, and ...c5 would be needed to open it at the cost of another tempo. Meanwhile White takes the centre.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 b5.strategy: Challenges c4, but after cxb5 cxb5 the b5-pawn is loose: e4 opens the f1-bishop against it, and Qb3 and Nc3 hit it too. Black spends further moves holding the pawn while the pieces stay at home.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 e5.strategy: Hits d4 at once, but after 3.dxe5 the quickest way to win the pawn back is ...Qa5+ and ...Qxe5. With the queen in the open White gains tempi with its developing moves, and Black falls behind in development.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 f6.strategy: Prepares ...e5, but takes f6 from the knight and weakens e6 and the e8-h5 diagonal. White develops and claims the centre first.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 h6.strategy: Takes g5 from the bishop but is a slow rook-pawn move that develops nothing. White develops freely and has the centre to itself.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 h5.strategy: A flank advance that weakens g5 and g6 and does nothing for the centre or development. White builds the centre and may settle a bishop on g5.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 c5.strategy: Spends a second tempo on the c-pawn. After 3.d5 White has a space advantage a tempo up, and after 3.dxc5 Black needs more time to regain the pawn.

1.c4 c6 2.d4 g5.strategy: Hangs a pawn: Bxg5 takes it for nothing, since the e7-pawn blocks the queen's guard. Neither ...Qb6, hitting b2 and d4, nor ...Qa5+, hitting g5, wins it back, because Qd2 answers both.
